summary.title: Build Your Own Database
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a simple on-disk database in C# by layering block storage, variable-length record storage, and a disk-based B-Tree index.
takeaways: Store data in a single file split into fixed-size blocks, with a metadata header per block for links, content length and deleted flag.
Build variable-length records as linked lists of blocks, and reuse deleted block IDs via a stack kept in record #0.
Implement a disk-based B-Tree by serializing nodes into records and referencing other nodes by ID rather than memory pointers.
Combine record storage with primary (Guid) and secondary (Breed, Age) indexes to answer find, delete, update and search operations.
summary.summary: The author wants a database that stays fast as data grows, reuses deleted space and avoids SQLite's vacuum() step, for storing about a million records of 1KB-8KB. The design has three layers: BlockStorage splits one file into equal-size blocks (4KB chosen), RecordStorage chains blocks into variable-length records and recycles freed block IDs, and an on-disk B-Tree index maps keys to record IDs. The article walks through the interfaces, the implementation details and a demo "CowDatabase" in C#, with notes on caching, performance on mono and a write-caching issue. The project is presented as a 24-32 hour learning exercise without ACID or transactions.
